Hi Elaine —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front: we can share our SOC 2 Type II report and a bridge letter; we also include an evidence manifest that describes what artifacts were reviewed. Below is what we typically provide and a short reply template you can paste into your procurement portal.

What Redwood typically shares (redacted where appropriate):
- Final SOC 2 Type II report (PDF) with auditor name and covered period.
- Evidence manifest (CSV) listing sampled control evidence (logs, config snapshots, runbooks) and retention windows.
- Optional bridge letter (Word/PDF) confirming status between report end date and delivery date.
- Standard redaction guidance: we can remove customer-identifying artifacts and any sensitive third-party IP; we do not redact control descriptions or auditor opinion.

Preferred transfer methods (pick one):
- Google Drive secure folder (service-account access + limited TTL link) — fastest.
- SFTP with a dedicated account — good for bulk artifacts.
- Vendor portal (we can upload to your secure intake if you provide portal credentials).

Quick reply template you can use: 
"""
Redwood Inference has provided their latest SOC 2 Type II report (audit firm and period included), an evidence manifest describing sampled artifacts, and a bridge letter to cover the gap between the report period and expected contract start. Materials will be transferred via a secure Google Drive link (or SFTP per vendor preference). Any customer-identifying data has been redacted.
"""

Action items for us: Ben — please propose transfer options and narrow to one; Marissa — we'll prepare the report PDF, manifest, and a bridge-letter draft for review.

I attached a recommended manifest template (evidence_manifest_2027-04-10.csv) we can populate. Let me know which transfer option Starlake prefers and any non-disclosure constraints.

Regards,
David Kim
Head of Partnerships (Security Intake Lead)
Redwood Inference

Elaine —

Thanks — cc'ing Marissa to coordinate the package. Options and steps from our side: 

Option A (recommended, fastest): Google Drive secure folder- we create a service account with viewer access and grant your security@starlake.ai account for 7 days. Pros: simple, supports large files. Cons: requires Google account for the service ACL.

Option B: SFTP - we provision a time-limited SFTP account and upload the artifacts. Pros: great for automation and large bulk transfers. Cons: requires firewall IP allowlist if you run strict egress policies.

Option C: Direct upload to your vendor portal - we can upload if you send an intake link or user credentials (we prefer scoped, short-lived credentials).

Checklist we will follow when assembling artifacts:
- Confirm report PDF includes auditor name and exact audit period.
- Populate evidence_manifest_2027-04-10.csv with artifact file names, control mapping, and redaction flags.
- Draft bridge letter (redwood_bridge_letter_2027-04-12.docx) that includes statement of ongoing controls and target remediation windows, for your legal review.
- Indicate any attachments that contain third-party vendor redactions.

Please confirm preferred transfer method and any IP/firewall addresses for SFTP allowlisting. Once you confirm, we'll schedule the upload window (we can do tomorrow morning US-PST).

Ben Carter
Security & Compliance Ops, Redwood Inference
Phone: 650-555-0122
